scope: Bounded primary-source engineering review and inherited settlement products; source identity and reading coverage recorded separately from forecasts.

sources.title: Large-scale Demonstration of Molten Regolith Electrolysis for Oxygen Production in a Relevant Environment
sources.coverage: Presentation slides 5–16, including equipment, nine-hour experiment and remaining development work.
sources.supports: 25 kg simulant, about 9 kW, 0.07 kg oxygen/hour in vacuum. These demonstrate a small reactor, not industrial metal quality, continuous production or the assumed 35 kWh/kg metal.

sources.title: NASA Office of Technology, Policy, and Strategy, Space Based Solar Power, January 2024
sources.coverage: Executive summary and selected manufacturing, assembly and renewal tables. No full-report reading claimed.
sources.supports: Conceptual 2050 systems and large uncertainty; example system masses 5.9 and 10 million kg per 2 GW design. Study prices are FY2022 dollars and are not copied into the 2026 price inputs.

sources.title: Glavin et al., Abundant ammonia and nitrogen-rich soluble organic matter in samples from asteroid (101955) Bennu, Nature Astronomy 9, 199–210
sources.coverage: Abstract and main-article sample/composition passages, including 4.5–4.7 wt% C and 0.23–0.25 wt% N. NASA-hosted PDF obtained after publisher access failed. Text extraction reports an annotation problem on page 21; supplementary material and full article not reviewed.
sources.supports: Measured chemical precedent for the nitrogen grade; not an extractable reserve, accessible flight target, water yield or approval to mine Bennu.

sources.title: Department of Energy technical targets for PEM electrolysis
sources.supports: 2022 system status 55 kWh/kg H2 and $1,000/kW uninstalled; ultimate targets 46 kWh/kg and $150/kW. These exclude installation and space adaptation. Model uses 55–80 kWh/kg including liquefaction and a separate space-plant allowance.

sources.title: Optical Mining of Asteroids, Moons, and Planets to Enable Sustainable Human Exploration and Space Industrialization
sources.supports: Small optical-mining vacuum experiments and proposed scale-up. No operational asteroid mine.

sources.title: Dressler et al., Test results from a simple, low-cost, pressure-fed liquid hydrogen/liquid oxygen rocket combustor
sources.coverage: NTRS abstract; no downloadable paper available in that record.
sources.supports: Hot-fire mixture ratios 5.8–8.4 and an adjusted 430 s vacuum result for a particular engine/nozzle. Does not demonstrate 430 s at mixture eight with the long reusable life assumed here.

sources.title: Experimental demonstration of a water electrolysis Hall Effect Thruster (WET-HET) operating with a hydrogen cathode
sources.coverage: Indexed publisher abstract and highlights; direct publisher page returned 403. No full-paper reading or numerical transfer of the reported krypton-cathode efficiency to hydrogen.
sources.supports: Laboratory oxygen/hydrogen operation using bottled gases. The 2,000 s and 30–50 percent total efficiency comparison is a future design assumption, not a qualified megawatt engine.

sources.title: Fortescue signs US$2.8 billion green equipment partnership with Liebherr
sources.supports: 475 machines including roughly 360 autonomous battery trucks, 55 electric excavators and 60 dozers; historical package price only, not a unit quotation or demonstration of independent lunar maintenance.

sources.title: SpaceX Smallsat Rideshare Program
sources.coverage: Current indexed first-party page text, retrieved 12 November 2026.
sources.supports: $350,000 for 50 kg to sun-synchronous orbit and $7,000/kg additional mass. This is a smallsat service, not a comparable bulk launch contract. The $50–1,000/kg future launch scenarios are assumptions.

retrieval_issues: The SpaceX Capabilities and Services PDF URL redirected to its homepage; no Falcon 9 numerical price input is taken from that failed retrieval.
Publisher access to the water-Hall paper failed; only its indexed abstract is used.
